user.title: Set up Brilliant MQTT
user.description: Choose where the Brilliant panels should connect. The recommended path uses the official Home Assistant Mosquitto broker add-on; an existing or externally hosted MQTT broker is also fully supported.

menu_options.existing_broker: Existing or external MQTT broker (fully supported)

official_mosquitto.title: Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on (recommended)
official_mosquitto.description: Use the official `core_mosquitto` add-on. Install and start the add-on first, then create dedicated Brilliant broker credentials for the panels. Home Assistant's existing MQTT connection is validated separately.

existing_broker.title: Existing or external MQTT broker
existing_broker.description: Use any reachable MQTT broker, including one hosted outside Home Assistant. The integration validates connectivity and required broker behavior before it changes a panel.

broker.title: Validate MQTT broker
broker.description: For the recommended Home Assistant path, install and start the official `core_mosquitto` add-on, then create dedicated Brilliant broker credentials before continuing. External-broker users do not need this add-on; enter a broker address reachable by Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel. You may also enable Home Assistant control and Brilliant scenes before the first panel is installed. Advanced settings are optional. [Open troubleshooting]({documentation_url})

data.ha_control_enabled: Enable Home Assistant control and scenes

data_description.mqtt_host: Address reachable by both Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel.
data_description.mqtt_port: Usually 1883 without TLS or 8883 with TLS.
data_description.mqtt_username: Broker account used by the Brilliant fleet.
data_description.mqtt_password: Broker password. It is stored securely and is never shown again.
data_description.ha_control_enabled: Optional. Enable the constrained Home Assistant MQTT control manifest and Brilliant scene bridge before the first panel is installed. This defaults off.

data_description.mqtt_tls_ca: Optional public PEM certificate chain for a private broker CA. Never paste a private key.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure panel
reconfigure.description: Edit this panel and the fleet-wide Home Assistant control settings. Panel changes are pushed over SSH; global settings are copied to every Brilliant entry.

data_description.voice: Install a Home Assistant voice satellite on this panel (on-panel wake word + microphone + speaker). Speech-to-text, the conversation agent, and text-to-speech all run in your HA Assist pipeline — nothing voice-specific is configured on the panel.
data_description.voice_wake_word: The on-panel wake word that activates the satellite.
data_description.voice_ha_host: Only needed if the panel cannot resolve your Home Assistant URL's hostname (e.g. a segmented IoT VLAN). Format: hostname=ip, e.g. homeassistant.example=10.0.0.5. Leave blank to use the panel's own DNS.
data_description.wifi_watchdog: Auto-recovers lost Wi-Fi (reconnect → restart networking → reboot the panel as a last resort).
data_description.bus_watchdog: Installs the on-panel daemon that reboots the panel if the Brilliant bus stays wedged for 30+ minutes.
data_description.hue_ca: Installs a periodic timer that re-injects your diyHue CA certificate into the panel's pinned Hue trust bundle, recovering it after an OTA update wipes /data.
data_description.hue_ca_cert: The diyHue bridge's CA certificate, PEM-encoded. Required to enable Hue CA recovery.
data_description.ha_control_enabled: Publishes a constrained, local MQTT control manifest from Home Assistant. The legacy on-panel HA mirror remains disabled.
data_description.ha_control_label: Home Assistant label selecting entities for the constrained control manifest.
data_description.room_overrides: A JSON object mapping Home Assistant area names to Brilliant room names, for example {"Office":"Office Bath"}.
data_description.ha_control_domains: Only selected supported domains enter the control manifest.
data_description.max_mirrored_entities: Safety limit for entities in the control manifest (1–200).
data_description.scene_panel: Brilliant panel used when a scene or mode service call omits a panel.
data_description.scene_actions: A JSON object of explicitly allowlisted scene actions keyed by panel and scene ID.

progress.broker_validation: Checking Home Assistant MQTT readiness, broker authentication, discovery writes, and retained-message behavior.

panel_connect.title: Connect to a Brilliant panel
panel_connect.description: Enter the panel address and root password. Home Assistant first reads and verifies the panel identity; installation starts only after you review the detected panel. [Open troubleshooting]({documentation_url})

data_description.host: A stable address reachable from Home Assistant.
data_description.root_password: Used only for this panel's pinned SSH connection and stored per panel.

panel_confirm.title: Confirm Brilliant panel
panel_confirm.description: Detected `{hostname}` ({model}, {architecture}) with SSH fingerprint `{fingerprint}`. Name the panel to continue. Home Assistant will verify durable fleet storage before making any panel changes. [Open troubleshooting]({documentation_url})

data_description.name: A friendly name used in Home Assistant. A stable MQTT slug is allocated automatically.

reconfigure.title: Manage Brilliant panel
reconfigure.description: Choose one focused panel operation. Identity-sensitive changes are verified against the panel's pinned SSH identity before anything is saved.

rename.title: Rename panel
rename.description: Change only the panel's display name. Its MQTT slug, entity identities, pinned SSH identity, and settings stay unchanged.

data_description.name: Friendly name shown in Home Assistant. Renaming does not change MQTT topics or entity IDs.

address.title: Change panel network address
address.description: Move this panel to a new hostname or IP address. Home Assistant accepts the address only if it presents the panel's existing pinned SSH identity.

data.host: New panel IP address or hostname

data_description.host: Stable address reachable from Home Assistant. Use Replace physical panel instead if the SSH identity is different.

repair_credentials.title: Repair panel SSH credentials
repair_credentials.description: Replace the stored root password for this panel. Home Assistant verifies the existing pinned SSH identity before it offers the new password to the host.

data_description.root_password: The new password is stored only after authentication succeeds and is never shown again.

components.title: Manage installed components
components.description: Component switches and selectors live with this panel's Home Assistant device so their state and failures remain observable.

overrides.title: Edit panel feature overrides
overrides.description: Set supported voice and certificate values before enabling their component. For an active Voice satellite, change the wake word with its selector; disable Voice or Hue CA recovery before changing another value, then enable it again. Fleet repair behavior and pinned identity are not changed.

data_description.voice_wake_word: Wake word used on the next Voice satellite install. If Voice is active, use the panel's Wake word selector instead.
data_description.voice_ha_host: Optional hostname=IP mapping for a panel that cannot resolve the Home Assistant hostname. Disable Voice before changing this active value; leave blank to use panel DNS.
data_description.hue_ca_cert: Optional public PEM certificate chain for diyHue CA recovery. Disable Hue CA recovery before changing its active certificate. Never paste a private key.

rebind.title: Replace physical panel
rebind.description: Use this only when intentionally replacing the physical panel represented by this Home Assistant device. Home Assistant reads the replacement's SSH identity before authentication and inspects it read-only. No panel settings or stored identity are changed until you review and confirm the detected replacement.

data.host: Replacement panel IP address or hostname

data_description.host: Stable address of the replacement panel, reachable from Home Assistant.
data_description.root_password: Used only after the replacement SSH identity is captured. It is never redisplayed.

rebind_confirm.title: Confirm physical panel replacement
rebind_confirm.description: Detected replacement `{hostname}` ({model}, {architecture}) with SSH fingerprint `{new_fingerprint}`. The currently pinned fingerprint is `{old_fingerprint}`. Confirm only if you intentionally replaced this physical panel. This replaces the pinned SSH identity while preserving the logical panel's MQTT slug, entities, name, components, and feature settings.

data.confirm: I confirm this is the intended replacement panel

data_description.confirm: Home Assistant rechecks the replacement identity immediately before saving. Leave this off to make no changes.

progress.panel_provision: Inspecting, staging, validating, activating, and health-checking the panel. If any step fails, the prior panel state is restored automatically.

init.title: Brilliant MQTT settings
init.description: Manage fleet-owned MQTT, Home Assistant control, scene, and repair settings. Legacy panel entries show their supported behavior fields here.

data.auto_repair: Automatically repair the bridge after an outage

data_description.trust_host_key_changes: When on, repair auto-trusts a changed SSH host key so a firmware update that rotates the panel's keys recovers hands-off. This offers the root password to whatever host answers at the panel's address, so only enable on a trusted/isolated network (e.g. a firewalled IoT VLAN). Each automatic re-pin fires a host_key_repinned event you can alert on. Default off: a changed key instead surfaces repair_failed (host_key_changed) and asks you to Reconfigure to re-pin.

broker.title: Choose MQTT broker guidance
broker.description: Select the broker setup you use. The choice changes onboarding guidance only; both paths use the same validated MQTT transport.

menu_options.existing_broker: Existing or external MQTT broker (fully supported)

official_mosquitto.title: Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on (recommended)
official_mosquitto.description: Use the official `core_mosquitto` add-on after installing and starting it and creating dedicated Brilliant broker credentials.

existing_broker.title: Existing or external MQTT broker
existing_broker.description: Use any broker reachable by Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel. The same connectivity, authentication, ACL, discovery, and retained-message checks validate this fully supported path.

broker_profile.title: Validate MQTT broker settings
broker_profile.description: The official `core_mosquitto` add-on is the recommended Home Assistant default, but it is not required. An existing or externally hosted broker is fully supported. Broker changes are validated before being saved; installed panels require the guided rollout described in the MQTT broker setup documentation. [Open troubleshooting]({documentation_url})

data_description.mqtt_host: Address reachable by Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel.
data_description.mqtt_port: Usually 1883 without TLS or 8883 with TLS.
data_description.mqtt_username: Dedicated MQTT account used by the Brilliant fleet.
data_description.mqtt_password: Leave the masked value unchanged to keep the stored password, or enter a replacement password.

data_description.mqtt_tls_enabled: Encrypt MQTT transport and verify the broker certificate.
data_description.mqtt_tls_ca: Optional public PEM certificate chain for a private broker CA. Never paste a private key.

broker_validation.title: Validating MQTT broker
broker_validation.description: Home Assistant is checking MQTT readiness, fleet authentication, bidirectional traffic, discovery writes, retained messages, and cleanup before saving anything.

broker_commit.title: Saving MQTT broker settings
broker_commit.description: Home Assistant is rechecking fleet ownership and the validated broker snapshot before the durable update.

ha_control.title: Home Assistant control
ha_control.description: Configure the constrained MQTT control manifest once for the fleet. Changing whether control is enabled after panels are installed requires a guided agent rollout; the other fields update live.

data_description.ha_control_enabled: Publish the constrained local MQTT control manifest. The legacy on-panel Home Assistant mirror remains disabled.
data_description.ha_control_label: Home Assistant label selecting entities for the fleet control manifest.
data_description.room_overrides: JSON object mapping Home Assistant area names to Brilliant room names, for example {"Office":"Office Bath"}.
data_description.ha_control_domains: Only entities in these supported domains can enter the control manifest.
data_description.max_mirrored_entities: Fleet safety limit from 1 through 200 entities.

scenes.title: Scenes and modes
scenes.description: Choose the current panel that owns default scene requests and maintain the explicit scene-action allowlist. At least one panel must be configured.

data_description.scene_panel: Panel used when a scene or mode service call does not specify one. The saved owner is its stable Home Assistant panel ID.
data_description.scene_actions: JSON object of explicitly allowed actions keyed by immutable panel MQTT slug and scene ID.

fleet_defaults.title: Fleet repair defaults
fleet_defaults.description: Set the repair timing defaults inherited by panels that do not have an explicit per-panel override. SSH host-key trust is never changed here.

data_description.auto_repair: Allow the manager to repair an unhealthy panel automatically after its offline grace period.
data_description.offline_grace_minutes: Wait from 2 through 120 minutes before treating a panel outage as actionable.
data_description.repair_cooldown_minutes: Wait from 5 through 1440 minutes between automatic repair attempts.

advanced.title: Advanced fleet operations
advanced.description: These operations can affect panel-wide behavior and require extra safety checks.

mesh_priorities.title: Mesh priority rollout required
mesh_priorities.description: Mesh priority changes alter on-panel agent configuration and are available only through a journaled rollout. Direct mutation is intentionally blocked.

progress.broker_validation: Validating Home Assistant MQTT readiness, broker authentication, bidirectional fleet topics, discovery writes, retained messages, and cleanup.

error.retained_message_timeout: Retained-message validation timed out. Check broker persistence, routing, and ACL behavior, then retry.
error.cleanup_failed: MQTT validation cleanup could not be confirmed. Check broker availability and ACLs before retrying.

mode_id.description: Stable mode ID from the selected panel's current catalog.

already_in_progress.message: A repair or update is already in progress for this panel.

host_key_changed.message: The panel SSH host key changed. For a fleet panel, verify the physical replacement and use Replace physical panel for an explicit identity rebind. Legacy entries may be removed and re-added after verification, or may use "Trust host-key changes" only on a trusted isolated network. If the change is unexpected, investigate the address and network before proceeding.

needs_attention.title: Brilliant panel needs attention
needs_attention.description: Panel `{panel}` needs attention: {reason}. This issue clears automatically once the bridge recovers.

voice_missing.title: Brilliant panel voice satellite not installed
voice_missing.description: Panel `{panel}` has the voice satellite enabled but it isn't running. This issue clears automatically once the satellite is deployed (run Repair, or wait for the next automatic repair).

ha_mirror_retired.title: Legacy Brilliant HA mirror disabled
ha_mirror_retired.description: Panel `{panel}` still has legacy HA mirror state. {reason}. The integration will keep retrying safe removal during panel management; legacy credentials are retained until absence is verified.
